name: Refugee Status / International Protection

requirements.blocker_text: Meets the refugee definition applied under Jamaica's National Refugee Policy (2009) -- a well-founded fear of persecution on protected grounds, per the 1951 Refugee Convention standard Jamaica has adopted.

sources.title: Jamaica Information Service (JIS) -- ministerial/official statements confirming Jamaica has adopted a National Refugee Policy (2009), described as the only codified refugee policy of its kind in the English-speaking Caribbean

UNHCR -- Caribbean regional overview: lists Jamaica's refugee status determination as administered under a distinct local government procedure rather than a UNHCR-mandate RSD process, unlike several other Caribbean states in this dataset

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Jamaica). STATUS: DRAFT -- kept draft despite tier-1/tier-2 sourcing because the primary 2009 National Refugee Policy document itself, and the specific eligibility criteria, procedural steps, and rights granted to recognized refugees, could not be located at tier-1 or tier-2 in this build. What is confirmed: Jamaica runs its OWN domestic refugee status determination under a codified national policy -- UNHCR's own regional categorization places Jamaica under 'local government procedure' rather than UNHCR-mandate-administered RSD, distinguishing it from several other Caribbean states. This is a genuine, disclosed sourcing gap rather than an invented eligibility structure: the single hard requirement here is modeled at the level of the general Convention-standard refugee definition Jamaica is understood to apply, not confirmed against the policy's own text. Top re-verification priority: locate the 2009 National Refugee Policy document directly, likely via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade (MFAFT) or PICA. SCHEMA NOTE: renewable/family_can_join/leads_to_pr/leads_to_citizenship are non-nullable fields in this dataset's schema, so conservative defaults (renewable=true, family_can_join=false, leads_to_pr=false, leads_to_citizenship=false) are used here rather than left blank -- these are NOT independently confirmed and should not be read as sourced facts, only as schema-compliant placeholders pending the primary policy document.
